title: InfinityStar: Uniﬁed Spacetime AutoRegressive Modeling for Visual Generatio

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states: 'Without extra optimizations, our model generates a 5s, 720p video approximately 10× faster than leading diffusion-based methods.' However, Table 6 reports that InfinityStar generates a 5s 720p video in 58 s, while the diffusion method Wan 2.1 takes 1864 s, giving a speedup of about 32×, not 10×. The abstract's claim directly contradicts the experimental results presented in the paper.

predicted_errors.error_location: Equation (2) and surrounding text in Section 3.2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states that 'clips are generated sequentially conditioned on prior clip predictions and the text input in an autoregressive manner.' However, Equation (2) is written as p(r_1^1, ..., r_K^N) = ∏_{c=1}^N ∏_{k=1}^K p(r_k^c | r_1^c, ..., r_{k-1}^c, ψ(t)), which conditions only on the current clip's earlier scales and the text, but omits any conditioning on tokens from previous clips. This makes the equation inconsistent with the described inter-clip autoregressive generation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.4, 'Spacetime Sparse Attention' paragraph, speedup claims vs. Table 5
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text claims 'SSA reaches 1.5× speedup when generating 192p 16f' and later mentions '1.1× and 1.5× speedup for 192p and 480p 16f'. However, Table 5 shows for (192p 65 frames) a speedup of only ~1.12× (8.6 s vs. 7.7 s), and for 480p 16f (appearing as 480p 161 frames in the table) full attention runs out of memory, so no speedup can be computed. The stated speedup figures are not supported by the timing data in the table and appear to be incorrectly reported or derived from a different configuration not described.
